To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) temporal SQL is upward compatible with conventional SQL if and only if it satisfies the three notions of upward compatibility; (2) no existing temporal SQL is upwardly compatible with conventional SQL; and (3) SQL–92 can easily be extended to become an upwardly compatible temporal query language.

(1) there is a systematic way of extending SQL–92 to obtain a temporal query language; (2) the temporal extensions to SQL–92 in the literature are all incompatible with conventional SQL; and (3) the temporal extensions in the literature are incompatible with one another.

1) the temporal extensions to SQL–92 that have been proposed to date are not upward compatible, 2) a temporal extension to SQL–92 can easily be devised that satisfies all three of these notions, 3) the temporal extension to SQL that is proposed here is upward compatible, and 4) a temporal extension that is upward compatible is more useful than a non-upward-compatible one for the purposes of migrating legacy applications to a new temporal database management system.
